doc.title: Sonny Igoe interviewed by Monk Rowe, Emerson, New Jersey, July 31, 2003

chapter: Studio years and changing rock rhythms
title: Rock and roll opinions and Pee Wee Erwin
summary: Igoe admits stubbornness about rock, recalls Pee Wee Erwin's quip, and praises rock drummers but not the music.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: I didn’t. I was stubborn. I was very stubborn. And I said oh it will never happen. Those guys can’t play. Listen to that, they can’t even play an ending. Every record fades out. They can’t even play an ending. None of them can play. But everybody said hey Sonny, you’ve got to get onto this. So okay. So then it happens that with my good friend Pee Wee Irwin and we were going out to play a jazz gig out in Pennsylvania and I’m driving and Pee Wee and I are chatting. Now this is not to be derogatory to any specific group of people except rock & rollers I guess. So anyway we’re talking about the state of the music business. And we’re talking about the inroads that rock & rollers made in radio and everything, that’s all you hear, because this was in the 70s. And I said, “Jesus, Pee Wee, that’s all you hear.” And he says, “well you have to admit one thing, Sonny, rock & roll is putting all the amateurs to work.” And I never forgot that. And there are guys in rock & roll who can really play, there’s no doubt about it. And I like a lot of the drummers I hear in some rock groups. I can’t name one right now. But I hate the music they have to play. But I say, “geez, listen to that, that kid can play.” Because I know what drums sound like,

I don’t care what style it is, if you’re going to play Latin if you’re playing lousy I’m going to know it. But some of these guys are really good but the music, oh God, terrible. That’s only my opinion folks.
